# Refresh Chromium launch defaults for Playwright 1.65

## Context

Dependabot PR #20608 updates Playwright from 1.64.1 to 1.65.0 and Mermaid from 12.2.0 to 12.3.0. Its [unit job](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42521125847/job/128854709340) fails the same disabled-feature parity assertion on all three attempts: `test/playwright/unit/e2e/glState.spec.mjs:133`. The main tier reports 6,655 passed, 3 skipped and one failure; both timezone tiers pass.

The operator explicitly requested applying the prepared patch to that existing PR before the release cut. This is one maintainer repair on the existing dependency change.

## The Problem

The checked-in `PLAYWRIGHT_DISABLED_FEATURES` copy still matches 1.64.1. [Playwright 1.65.0's exact source](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.65.0/packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/chromiumSwitches.ts) removes five entries and adds three. Its 16-entry list and Neo's 18-entry copy therefore differ.

Chrome uses the last `--disable-features` argument. Neo repeats Playwright's list before adding its own three features, so stale copy drift can re-enable upstream-disabled behavior. The equality guard is intentional; the copy and dependency version must land together.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/e2e/utils/gpuIntent.mjs` owns the literal copy and one combined launch argument. Both engine and presenting profiles derive it.
- `test/playwright/unit/e2e/glState.spec.mjs` reads the installed Playwright bundle and requires exact copy equality and one combined argument in each profile.
- Design authority: the existing module JSDoc says `glState.spec.mjs` fails when installed Playwright's list stops matching. The retained contract on #19675 explicitly requires a dependency upgrade to fail until the copy follows.
- Closed #19755 and #19863 are earlier version-specific repairs, not open owners of this new upgrade.

## The Fix

Refresh only the literal copy, in upstream order, on the existing PR #20608:
- Add `HttpsFirstBalancedModeAutoEnable`, `TcpPortRandomizationWin`, `PreconnectToSearch`.
- Remove `DialMediaRouteProvider`, `GlobalMediaControls`, `BlockOriginHeaderModificationOnRedirect`, `Translate`, `AutoDeElevate`.

Keep Neo's `IsolateOrigins`, `site-per-process` and `TouchpadOverscrollHistoryNavigation` additions, the profile distinctions and the unchanged parity guard.

Prescription checked: `gpuIntent.mjs` owns the declaration; an independent source read confirms no runner, renderer or production config change is needed. Retain manual merge for this mixed bot/maintainer PR: its workflow disarms auto-merge on non-Dependabot synchronization, and verify that state after push.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Edge case / docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disabled-feature copy | Selected installed Playwright; existing JSDoc | Exact 1.65.0 list | Future upstream drift keeps failing | Existing parity arm, red before repair |
| Launch profiles | Existing BASE_LAUNCH_ARGS | One argument with upstream list plus the three Neo additions | Engine/presenting differences unchanged | Full glState unit file and standalone profile controls |

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The selected 1.65.0 dependency passes the unchanged parity assertion with the updated literal copy.
- [ ] Both profiles retain exactly one combined argument, all upstream entries and the three Neo additions; other profile flags are unchanged.
- [ ] The full existing glState unit file passes, with the old-copy mismatch retained as the red control.
- [ ] The fix is appended to #20608, its exact-head required CI is rechecked, and auto-merge remains disarmed for human review/merge.

## Out of Scope

Changing the copy/guard design, dynamic production imports from Playwright's private bundle, weakening tests, unrelated source changes, new dependency PRs, a version/release cut or merge execution.

## Avoided Traps

An unchanged rerun cannot repair deterministic drift. Updating the copy on dev without its matching dependency would create the inverse mismatch. A second PR is unnecessary because the operator authorized applying the patch to the existing mixed change.
